When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.

At Parexel, we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.

Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.

The Principal Consultant, Pricing & Market Access at Parexel is responsible for leading a team of professionals to delivering strategic market access and commercialization solutions to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and specialty healthcare clients. The Principal Consultant serves as a trusted advisor to clients, leading complex engagements across pricing, reimbursement, HTA, value communications, evidence generation, launch readiness, and market access strategy.

Your focus will be to deliver client services whilst build trusted relationships with new existing and new clients to build the Parexel Access Consulting brand and reputation in the business.

Working within a CRO environment, the Principal Consultant collaborates closely with experts across clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), HEOR, medical, regulatory, and commercialization functions to deliver integrated solutions that support clients throughout the product lifecycle.

As a Principal within the Access team, you will work directly with clients to develop business opportunities and deliver project ensuring high client satisfaction. The role combines strategic consulting leadership, business development, project oversight, and team mentorship, while contributing to the growth and development of the Pricing & Market Access practice.


Your Expertise;

Essential Knowledge and Experience:

  • 6+ years Pricing & Market Access experience, in a consulting environment
  • 3+ years project management experience in pricing & market access and/or HTA and literature review projects with the ability to control projects from proposal through to delivery with successful client outcomes
  • Recognised as a trusted advisor within the market access and healthcare community, with the ability to translate industry relationships, market insight, and professional credibility into long-term client value and sustainable business growth.
  • A strong track-record of timely and high-quality project delivery, with demonstrable experience in producing client-ready deliverables that clearly show an understanding of client requirements

Desirable skills and experiences:

  • Experience in European HTA, pricing, and reimbursement processes, particularly within Germany (AMNOG) and/or France (HAS), is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop strategic market insights and client recommendations through deep expertise in EU and/or US market access environments, including HTA, pricing and reimbursement, healthcare policy, payer evidence requirements, claims data, and managed care analytics.

Education:

  • 2:1 or above Bachelor’s degree in a life science discipline, higher degree is desirable

Your Scope & Impact;


Strategic Client Advisory

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients on market access, payer, pricing, policy and reimbursement challenges.
  • Take ownership of client relationships, lead proposals, and seek out new opportunities
  • Lead collaborations with other businesses within Parexel to deliver client services and drive the development of new offerings
  • Lead the development of strategic recommendations across:
    • Global and regional market access landscape assessments
    • Pricing and market access strategy
    • Joint Clinical Assessment (JCA), HTA and reimbursement readiness and submission
    • Integrated Evidence Generation Planning (IEGP) and strategy
    • Payer value proposition development
    • Value communication materials, including value stories, global value dossiers and objection handlers
  • Advise clients on evolving access and policy environments, including:
    • EU HTAR and JCA requirements
    • UK and European HTA/reimbursement/pricing processes and policies
    • US payer and IRA-related considerations
    • International reference pricing dynamics

Project Leadership

  • Lead and oversee complex consulting engagements from proposal through delivery.
  • Provide strategic direction to multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Ensure delivery of high-quality, client-ready recommendations and deliverables.
  • Manage project scope, timelines, budgets, and client expectations and ensure accurate financial reporting
  • Identify and mitigate delivery risks while driving successful project outcomes.
  • Lead executive-level meetings, workshops, and presentations.
  • Works within broad project guidelines and facilitates issue and conflict resolutions.
  • Capitalizes on opportunities to improve project efficiency, results or team performance and proactively takes action

Project Examples

    • Pricing and reimbursement strategy
    • Launch sequencing and country prioritization
    • Payer evidence generation planning
    • HTA submission support
    • Payer research and advisory boards
    • Value dossier development
    • Evidence gap assessments
    • Access and reimbursement landscape analyses
    • Rare disease access strategy
    • Oncology market access planning
    • Cell and gene therapy commercialization planning

Business Development & Account Growth

  • Support new business generation through proposals, RFP responses, and client pitches.
  • Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships.
  • Develop a strong understanding of client priorities and unmet needs.
  • Develops business solutions addressing specific client needs using expertise, best practices and knowledge of the client’s business and key industry drivers
  • Collaborate with commercial leadership to drive account growth, through active prospecting, relationship building and identifying new business opportunities
  • Contribute to sales targets through direct and indirect business development activities.

Commercial Expectations

    • Generate and support NBA and revenue growth through proactive client engagement.
    • Contribute to new business opportunities across market access, HEOR, RWE, medical affairs, and evidence services.
    • Develop strong relationships with key client stakeholders. May act as a trusted advisor to clients, often on issues that lack precedence or are not clearly defined. May act as a loaned executive for a client

Cross-Functional Collaboration within the CRO

  • Work with the Access leadership team to lead the development and growth the global services
  • Work with a multifunctional team to support the engagement of clients across their development chain
  • Partner with colleagues across:
    • PMA, and HEOR
    • Real-World Evidence
    • Medical Communications
    • Clinical Development
    • Regulatory Consulting
    • Commercialization Services
  • Help clients connect evidence generation strategies with market access objectives.
  • Identify opportunities for integrated service offerings across the product lifecycle.
  • Promote collaboration across consulting and delivery teams to maximize client value.

Team Leadership & Development

  • Mentor consultants and senior consultants on strategic thinking, project delivery, and client engagement.
  • Provides a full range of technical and/or business consulting services within personal area of expertise including representing clients to regulatory agencies
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, and team capability development.
  • Provide coaching and constructive feedback to junior team members.
  • Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performance culture.
  • Serve as a role model for consulting excellence and professional development.

Thought Leadership

  • Contribute to the development of market access methodologies, tools, and intellectual property.
  • Support publication of white papers, articles, and conference content.
  • Represent the organization at industry conferences, including:
    • ISPOR
    • World EPA
    • HTA
    • DIA
    • World Orphan Drug Congress
    • Regional HTA and market access forums
  • To evaluate the global (US, Europe and APAC) market and its changing landscape and adapt, adjust and develop solutions to ensure coverage of pharmaceutical products
  • Monitor emerging trends in:
    • Pricing and reimbursement
    • HTA
    • JCA
    • Rare diseases
    • Oncology
    • RWE and HEOR
    • AI-enabled evidence generation

jobs.description:
As a leading financial services and healthcare technology company based on revenue, SS&C is headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, and has 27,000+ employees in 35 countries. Some 20,000 financial services and healthcare organizations, from the world's largest companies to small and mid-market firms, rely on SS&C for expertise, scale, and technology.

Job Description

Title: Migration Services Project Manager

Location: Remote

About the Team:

The Intralinks data migration team is the strategic growth lever for the company. By enabling Intralinks customers on Intralinks legacy products to upgrade to the newest Intralinks products and platforms, you will be the tip of the spear for the companies’ growth in 2022 and beyond. You’ll be part of a global team of experts in the Intralinks platform, FinTech, and cutting-edge new technologies.

About the Role:

This Migration Services Project Manager (MSPM) position will work with new and existing customers to ensure that they are satisfied and successful with Intralinks migration services. The MSPM will orchestrate the successful migration of these accounts from Intralinks legacy and competitor platforms onto new Intralinks platforms and products. The MSPM will coordinate multiple migrations, directly support, and assist in the delivery of migrations, train, lead, and mentor the Intralinks Migration Specialist team to deliver migrations and build high customer satisfaction. The MSPM will act as the voice of the customers internally within Intralinks. Creative, energetic and self-driven, the MSPM understands the customer’s existing Intralinks legacy implementations, and will be able to scope the migration level of effort, teach and train the Intralinks Migration Specialist staff to do the same. This position will be expected to manage 10-15 migrations at a time. The MSPM is expected to have an in- depth understanding of Intralinks’ legacy products and platforms to be migrated, as well as the new Intralinks products and platforms that are the target of these migrations.

Day to Day:

  • Ensure consistently positive customer experiences by providing oversight and project management for migration planning, project tracking, delivery, and technical issue resolution
  • Help to train and mentor Intralinks Migration Specialists on migration process and related Intralinks products and tools
  • Work with customer subject matter experts and Intralinks project team to identify, define, collate, document, and communicate data migration requirements
  • Synthesize customer migration requirements to estimate the migration level of effort and project plan and utilize this information to author migration SOW
  • Strategize and plan the entire Intralinks migration considering risks, timelines, and potential impacts
  • Oversee the entire migration process from legacy data mapping to QC of the migrated data, which may require unexpected adjustments to the process and schedule
  • Provide regular status updates to customer and Intralinks stakeholders
  • Document everything from the strategies used to the exact migration processes put in place—including documenting any fixes or adjustments made
  • Develop best practices, processes, and standards to continuously improve the Intralinks data migration process
  • Coordinate migration pipeline by educating, strategizing, and planning with account teams
  • Help to develop a continuous migration education and awareness program and coordinate training sessions as required
  • Troubleshoot and track product and migration tool issues with product management and engineering teams to ensure that critical migration issues are documented and escalated in an expeditious manner for resolution
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and guidelines for all migrated data

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in information management systems, computer science, or related field.
  • Relevant experience in project management and data migration
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, and presentation skills
  • Proficiency with MS Office applications including Excel, Word, Visio, Outlook, and Power Point
  • Ability to lead and direct a team of migration specialists

Desired Attributes

  • Detail oriented
  • Possess a clear, professional, friendly, and informative communication style
  • Enjoy creative problem and new challenges
  • Are a self-directed learner and highly motivated to succeed
  • Thrive in a dynamic startup environment, and are comfortable with ambiguity
  • Adapt quickly to changing priorities and evolving customer needs

It would be great if you also:

  • Experience with the Intralinks Platform
  • Demonstrated experience working in Alternative Investments, with an understanding on how business processes work within that vertical.
  • Proven knowledge of SaaS Alternative Investment and VDR solution technologies

Unless explicitly requested or approached by SS&C Technologies, Inc. or any of its affiliated companies, the company will not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services.

SS&C offers excellent benefits including health, dental, 401k plan, tuition and professional development reimbursement plan.

SS&C Technologies is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any applicant for employment or employee on the basis of race, color, religious creed, gender, age, marital status, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other classification protected by applicable discrimination laws.

jobs.excerpt: Be part of an amazing storyMacy’s is more than just a store.
jobs.description:
Be part of an amazing story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

The Senior, Project Management has direct responsibility for the administration and implementation of all assigned construction and capital projects. The Senior, Project Management coordinates with contracted suppliers and store management to ensure projects are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. The Senior, Project Management serves as the primary point of contact for the Store Environment teams, disseminating information and facilitating critical project decisions from inception to turnover. The role emphasizes improving the customer shopping experience and requires adaptability to change, consistently championing initiatives that reduce costs and save time. The Senior, Project Management demonstrates a strong sense of urgency and performs effectively under pressure in a collaborative team environment.

What You Will Do

  • Support the capital approval process, including budget and scope development, and preparation of phasing plans and project schedules.
  • Oversee construction, bidding, and administration processes in compliance with Capital Control policies and procedures. Participate in developing and maintaining construction cost estimates and forecasts, and manage ongoing budget tracking reports to ensure projects remain within budget.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with other Macy’s departments, including Stores, Strategic Procurement, Energy, Risk Management, Capital Planning, and Capital Control, demonstrating effective communication and collaboration skills.
  • Establish and maintain a network of competitive general contractors, subcontractors, and architectural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing service suppliers.
  • Lead strategic initiatives to refine and improve project operations and management processes.
  • Collaborate with store, district, and regional partners, as well as suppliers, to resolve property damage claims efficiently.
  • Support the Store Environment team and store organization in efforts to drive sales growth.
  • Mentor and coach Project Managers as needed or upon request.
  • Maintain regular, dependable attendance and punctuality.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships, and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.
  • In addition to the essential duties mentioned above, other duties may be assigned.

Skills You Will Need

Project & Construction Management: Ability to administer and implement construction and capital projects, oversee bidding and administration processes, and ensure completion on time, within budget, and to high-quality standards.

Financial Acumen: Skilled in budget development, cost estimation, forecasting, and ongoing budget tracking to ensure projects remain within financial parameters.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Builds and maintains strong relationships with internal departments (Stores, Strategic Procurement, Energy, Risk Management, Capital Planning, and Capital Control) and external partners (contractors, subcontractors, and service suppliers) to drive alignment and results.

Strategic Planning & Execution: Capable of developing phasing plans, project schedules, and strategic initiatives to refine and improve project operations and management processes.

Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Able to identify, assess, and resolve property damage claims, project issues, and operational challenges efficiently.

Communication & Presentation: Strong verbal and written communication skills; able to present information clearly to customers, leadership, and internal/external partners.

Adaptability & Initiative: Demonstrates flexibility in a fast-paced environment, champions new initiatives, reduces costs, and saves time.

Who You Are

  • Candidates with a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience in a related field are encouraged to apply. Master’s degree preferred.
  • This position requires heavy lifting, constant moving, remaining in a stationary position, and reaching with arms and hands. Involves remaining in a stationary position for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 30 lbs. stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders. May involve reaching above eye level. Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Able to work a flexible schedule, including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays, based on department and company needs.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice
  • Tuition reimbursement

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - apply today!

Moonlight is a boutique global staffing agency that places elite Executive Partners with US-based founders and CEOs. We don't do admin support; we build long-term, high-trust partnerships between exceptional operators and the executives who need them most. Our Executive Partners aren't assistants. They're captains in their own right, trusted to think ahead, own outcomes, and grow alongside the leaders they support.

The Role

As an Executive Partner, you'll be the strategic right hand to a US-based founder or CEO — anticipating needs before they're voiced, protecting their time like it's your own, and becoming the person they can't imagine running their business without. This isn't a task-execution role. It's a seat at the table.

What You'll Own

  • Strategic calendar and inbox management, triaging what matters, filtering out what doesn't
  • Executive-ready research, reports, and presentations that drive real decisions
  • Cross-functional coordination across the exec's business and personal priorities
  • Travel, logistics, and meeting coordination with zero dropped balls
  • Acting as a trusted gatekeeper and first point of contact on the exec's behalf
  • Proactively spotting opportunities to make the exec's life and business run better

Requirements

  • 3+ years supporting a founder/CEO or C-suite exec — ideally with progression from assistant into a chief-of-staff or Executive Partner–level role
  • End-to-end ownership, not single-task support — you've run inbox, calendar, CRM, and client comms as whole workflows, not waited for instructions
  • A named system, not just good instincts — a repeatable framework for inbox triage, calendar management, and prioritizing strategic vs. operational vs. urgent
  • Voice-matching ability — you can study how an exec writes and draft on their behalf convincingly
  • External representation experience — you've stood in for an exec on client calls, meetings, or board settings, not just scheduled them
  • Tool fluency that goes deep — CRM and task management platforms (Asana, Monday, ClickUp) you've configured, not just used
  • A real story of composure under pressure — a time something slipped, how you owned it, and what changed after
  • Evidence of moving up the value chain — building a tool, catching an issue early, proposing a project unprompted
  • A quantifiable track record — specific outcomes tied to your own contribution, not team results

Benefits

  • Probationary period (first 3 months): $800 USD/month (approx. 103,000 Kenyan Shilling)
  • Post-probationary: $1,000 USD/month (approx. 128,000 Kenyan Shilling)
  • Paid time off on all observed US Holidays
  • Health Benefit of up to $600 USD annually, active from month six

Why Moonlight

  • Global talent, global standards. We source Executive Partners worldwide — this isn't a single-market pipeline, it's a global bench of top-tier talent.
  • Real partnership, not gig work. You're matched long-term with one executive, not rotated across accounts.
  • Built-in growth path. Clear pay progression after probation, health coverage, and a team that invests in where you're headed next — not just what you can do today.
  • Boutique means personal. Small, high-touch team. You're never a ticket number.

Ready to become someone's indispensable right hand? Apply today and let's see if it's a match.

Moonlight is an equal opportunity employer sourcing talent globally. We evaluate every candidate on merit, judgment, and fit — not geography.

As a Director, Health Plans, this professional will own the full account relationship, serving as both the account executive and the day-to-day success owner for their clients. They will be responsible for a deep understanding of customer needs, fostering enduring relationships, and driving both growth and retention without a dedicated support layer as an Account Executive.


This is a hands-on role: the person in this seat is expected to run their own accounts, build their own analyses, and operate independently in a fast-moving, startup-paced environment. They will possess proven communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills, along with an analytical, results-driven approach focused on customer satisfaction and retention.


The role is eligible to anyone working remote within the U.S.

What your impact will be:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for an assigned book of health plan accounts, developing and nurturing proven relationships with clients.
  • Become experienced in each client's strategic business targets, book of business, and operations.
  • Increase customer engagement through a proactive cadence of check-ins; understand clients' evolving needs and identify opportunities for additional services.

  • Independently build the account-level analysis behind recommendations — including enrollment and portfolio data, opportunity sizing, and client-ready materials.

  • Facilitate or host webinars with experts to enhance customers' product knowledge.
  • Monitor contract renewals and proactively engage with clients to secure renewals.

Travel Requirements:


  • 5 - 10 % travel throughout the year

What we look for:


  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Computer Science, Data/Analytics, or a related field.

  • An analyst-caliber background, with the ability to work directly with data (e.g., Excel, SQL, BI tools) to build account insights independently. (1-3 years)

  • Prior experience in a startup or lean, high-ownership environment. (1-3 years)

  • Proven experience as an Account Executive, Customer Success Manager, or in a similar client-facing role carrying both relationship and commercial outcomes. (2-4 years)

  • Proven communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to understand technical concepts and translate them into client-friendly terms.

  • Results-driven with a focus on customer satisfaction and retention.

Salary Range:


  • $120 - 135K

What we offer:

  • Plenty of opportunities to grow your career
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits
  • 3 weeks of vacation plus 5 personal days to recharge
  • Employee stock ownership, RRSP program, 401k + matching
  • A chance to give back through community involvement
  • Flexible work arrangements to suit your lifestyle

For nearly two decades, ConnectureDRX’s vast network of health plan data has brought carriers, FMOs and brokers together to simplify selling health plans in order to help millions of consumers find and enroll in their best fit Medicare plans every year.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Growth & Lifecycle
jobs.excerpt: About Rhythm EnergyRhythm is a renewable energy and technology company redefining how people interact with energy.
jobs.description:
About Rhythm Energy

Rhythm is a renewable energy and technology company redefining how people interact with energy. We combine energy market expertise with technology, design, and data science to deliver simple, transparent, and customer-centric energy solutions.

We’re a mission-driven team focused on building scalable systems, solving complex problems, and making a meaningful impact on the future of energy.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Product Manager – Growth & Lifecycle to own the customer-facing products and experiences that bring customers to Rhythm and keep them here.

You’ll own the customer journey from enrollment through renewal, building products that make energy simpler and give customers the information they need to make confident decisions. We'll measure your success primarily by two outcomes: conversion and retention.

You’ll work closely with Marketing and our Head of Growth to identify opportunities and run experiments across the funnel, and with Product Design to create simple, intuitive customer experiences. You’ll own product requirements and final sign-off on customer-facing experiences before they move into development.

Churn reduction and retention are among Rhythm’s top product priorities, giving this role direct and visible impact on company results from day one.

We’re looking for an independent, decisive Product Manager who can lead the room, align stakeholders, make recommendations, and move decisions forward in a fast-paced environment.

What You’ll Do

Growth & Lifecycle Product Ownership

  • Own the roadmap for Rhythm’s customer-facing products across the lifecycle, including the enrollment journey, customer portal, retention, and renewal experiences.
  • Drive measurable improvements in conversion and retention, establishing clear success metrics for initiatives and reporting on outcomes.
  • Lead retention and churn reduction initiatives, identifying where customers drop off or disengage and building experiences designed to keep them with Rhythm.
  • Use customer data, funnel analytics, segmentation, and user feedback to understand customer behavior and identify the highest-impact opportunities.
  • Monitor product performance after launch and continuously iterate based on customer behavior and results.

Experimentation & Conversion

  • Partner closely with Marketing and the Head of Growth to turn growth opportunities into clear hypotheses and product experiments.
  • Design, prioritize, and run A/B tests across the customer journey, from acquisition and enrollment through engagement and renewal.
  • Use experimentation to evaluate messaging, workflows, offers, experiences, and other opportunities to improve conversion and retention.
  • Translate experiment results into clear product decisions and use learnings to inform what we build next.
  • Build a consistent experimentation practice where hypotheses, success metrics, results, and next steps are clearly defined.

Customer Experience & Product Design

  • Partner closely with Product Design to simplify customer experiences across Rhythm’s digital products.
  • Own final sign-off on customer-facing designs from a product workflow and requirements perspective before implementation.
  • Ensure customer experiences balance customer needs, business objectives, technical considerations, and measurable product outcomes.
  • Use qualitative and quantitative customer insights to identify friction and make experiences simpler, clearer, and easier to act on.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Delivery

  • Align stakeholders across Marketing, Sales, Operations, Customer Care, Analytics, Design, and Engineering around product priorities and decisions.
  • Bring clear recommendations to cross-functional conversations and drive decisions forward rather than waiting for consensus.
  • Translate business objectives and customer problems into clear product requirements, user stories, workflows, and success metrics.
  • Partner with Engineering throughout the software development lifecycle to manage delivery through our Agile process.
  • Communicate product strategy, priorities, tradeoffs, performance, and recommendations clearly to stakeholders and Executive Leadership.
  • Independently own your product area while maintaining strong alignment across the teams that contribute to the customer experience.

What You’ll Bring

  • 3+ years of Product Management experience, with a focus on growth, lifecycle, retention, or other B2C customer-facing products.
  • A track record of building and shipping customer-facing experiences that measurably improved conversion, retention, or engagement.
  • Hands-on experience designing, running, and interpreting A/B tests.
  • Strong understanding of conversion funnels and the customer behaviors that influence acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and renewal.
  • Experience working closely with UI/UX designers to create simple, intuitive customer experiences.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to align multiple teams, make recommendations, navigate competing priorities, and move decisions forward.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort using customer and product data to validate ideas, prioritize opportunities, and measure results.
  • Solid understanding of the software development lifecycle, including roadmap planning, PRDs, user stories, and Agile delivery.
  • Clear, direct, and concise communication skills, from day-to-day working sessions through Executive Leadership.
  • Ability to work independently and take full ownership of your product area in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in retail energy, utilities, or another subscription or recurring-billing business where you manage the customer relationship over time, such as SaaS, telecom, insurance, or FinTech.
  • Background in Product Marketing or Go-to-Market before moving into Product Management.
  • Exposure to customer lifecycle analytics, including churn, customer lifetime value (CLV), segmentation, and retention cohorts.
  • Experience using SQL and data tools such as Databricks, Tableau, Google Analytics, or FullStory.
  • Familiarity with experimentation platforms and Figma.
  • Experience conducting user interviews and combining qualitative customer feedback with quantitative data to inform product decisions.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months, success in this role will look like:

  • Enrollment conversion improves through product improvements, experimentation, and a better understanding of where customers experience friction.
  • Customer retention improves, and churn decreases across key customer segments.
  • Rhythm has a consistent, well-run experimentation practice with Marketing, where hypotheses and success metrics are clearly defined, and test results directly influence what we build next.
  • Customer-facing experiences become simpler, clearer, and easier for customers to understand and act on.
  • Product decisions are grounded in customer behavior, funnel analytics, experimentation, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Cross-functional meetings consistently end with clear decisions, owners, and next steps, with Product trusted to drive the process forward.
  • You independently own the Growth & Lifecycle roadmap and are trusted to identify opportunities, make recommendations, and move priorities forward.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Meaningful ownership. Own customer-facing products across the lifecycle, from enrollment through renewal.
  • Direct business impact. Conversion, retention, and churn are critical business priorities, and your work will directly influence each of them.
  • Experimentation at the core. Work closely with Marketing and Growth to test ideas, learn quickly, and use results to determine what we build next.
  • Customer-focused product development. Partner closely with Product Design to make complex energy experiences simpler and more intuitive.
  • Cross-functional exposure. Work across Marketing, Growth, Design, Engineering, Analytics, Sales, Operations, and Customer Care.
  • Our culture. We’re friendly, transparent, collaborative, and love to innovate together.
  • Professional development. We support continued learning and provide opportunities to grow alongside the business.
  • Competitive compensation and benefits. We offer competitive compensation, performance-based rewards, paid vacation, and comprehensive benefits.

Hiring Process

We aim to keep our interview process thoughtful, transparent, and respectful of your time.

  1. People Screen (30 minutes) – Meet with a Talent Acquisition Partner to learn more about Rhythm, the opportunity, and your background.
  2. Hiring Manager Interview (30 minutes) – Dive deeper into your Product Management experience, growth and lifecycle ownership, experimentation approach, and experience building customer-facing products.
  3. Case Study Presentation (60 minutes) – Work through and present a role-relevant product challenge, giving us an opportunity to understand how you structure problems, use data, make tradeoffs, and communicate product recommendations.
  4. Stakeholder Interview (30 minutes) – Meet with a key cross-functional partner to explore how you collaborate, influence decisions, navigate competing priorities, and operate across teams.
  5. C-Level Conversation with our CPO – Meet with Rhythm’s Chief Product Officer for a final conversation about your experience, product philosophy, and potential impact at Rhythm.
  6. Offer – If it’s a mutual fit, we’ll move forward with an offer and discuss next steps.

Upstart's Corporate FP&A team is seeking an experienced, execution-focused Finance Manager to support strategic finance for Upstart Bank. This role will own the bank's integrated financial model, lead financial forecasting and scenario analysis, support Bank Board and Asset Liability Committee (ALCO) reporting, and monitor the bank's financial performance, balance sheet, liquidity, and regulatory capital position.

As a Finance Manager, Bank Finance, you will serve as a key finance partner responsible for Upstart Bank's financial planning and forecasting processes. You'll work closely with Treasury, Risk, Accounting, Capital Markets, Product, and other cross-functional partners to develop reliable financial forecasts and translate complex banking and regulatory concepts into clear, actionable insights. This role offers significant exposure to executive leadership and the opportunity to help build the financial planning infrastructure for a growing digital bank.

    • Support strategic planning by evaluating new products, funding strategies, and balance sheet initiatives through financial modeling and scenario analysis

jobs.description:
Tiugo is the company behind CKEditor, TinyMCE, and Uploadcare: developer tools that power rich content creation inside thousands of applications worldwide.

Our primary audience is the builder, the developer architecting an application that needs an embedded, enterprise-grade content and AI layer, where governance, compliance, and control are not nice-to-haves but hard requirements.

Behind every one of our products is a genuinely good story about solving exactly that problem well. Most of the world hasn't heard it yet.

The storyteller we're looking for

Great product marketing for developer tools lives in two worlds at once, and most people are only comfortable in one. You're very comfortable in both.

  • With builders, you go deep: Our primary audience is the developer designing an application where an embedded content and AI layer has to hold up to enterprise governance, compliance, and control. You want to understand their architecture, their constraints, the trade-offs they're weighing. You ask good technical questions, you respect their time, and you earn trust by getting the details right. Hand-wavy marketing makes you wince.

  • With decision-makers, you zoom out: You can take that same product and tell a crisp business story to a CTO, a VP of Engineering, or a product leader, people who care less about the internals and more about velocity, risk, cost, and staying compliant and in control as they ship AI into production. You make the value obvious without dumbing it down.

Where you sit

You report to your brand's Head of Product Marketing and work inside a tight pod built around a single brand: product marketing, developer relations, and the product team. Each function keeps its own reporting line, DevRel within a central DevRel team, product managers within Product. But the three move in lockstep on one mission: make the brand impossible to ignore. You'll be in the room with the people building the product and the people talking to developers every day. The raw material for great stories is right there; your job is to shape it.

What you will do

  • Tell the technical story: Turn real product capability into messaging that's accurate, vivid, and credible to the builders staking an enterprise application on it, developers who need governance, compliance, and control baked in, not bolted on. Honesty and precision are how trust gets earned here.

  • Tell the business story: Translate that same product into the language of the people who sign off, the outcomes, the risk reduction, the AI-era advantage. Build the narratives, decks, and proof points that help close enterprise deals.

  • Drive launches that land: Plan and run product and feature launches end to end, in concert with DevRel, product, and Growth Marketing, so releases hit with real impact instead of a quiet blog post.

  • Create content across the spectrum: From deeply technical deep-dives and comparison pieces to executive one-pagers and build-versus-buy narratives, you choose the right depth for the right reader every time.

  • Go to the source: Talk to developers and buyers, sit close to product usage and win/loss patterns, and bring real voices, not assumptions, into everything the team ships.

  • Win the AI discovery layer: Help the brand show up sharply when developers and buyers research through AI tools and search. How we get cited and surfaced is part of the modern storyteller's job.

  • Sharpen the edge: Know the competitors and alternatives cold, and arm the team with positioning that makes clear where this brand wins and why.

Requirements

What we are looking ror

  • +5 years in product marketing, technical content, DevRel-adjacent, or product roles, in B2B software, developer tools, or technical products.

  • A genuinely great writer and storyteller who can flex from deeply technical to plainly strategic, and knows which one a given audience needs.

  • Real curiosity about how things work. You enjoy going deep with engineers and you don't fake technical understanding, you build it.

  • The business instinct to see past features to outcomes, and to frame technology, especially AI, as the answer to a buyer's actual problem.

  • AI-fluent in how you work: you use AI tools to research, draft, and ship faster, and you're energized by how AI is reshaping both our products and how buyers discover them.

  • Rigor and care: you check your facts, sweat the details, and take pride in getting it right.

  • A fast, collaborative operator who thrives in a cross-functional team and doesn't wait to be told exactly what to do.

  • Bonus: experience with PLG / self-serve products, developer marketing, or a multi-brand portfolio.

Why this might be the role for you

  • Stories worth telling: real products developers genuinely love, with substance behind every claim. You'll never have to manufacture hype for something hollow.

  • A front-row seat to the craft: work shoulder to shoulder with the people building the product and learn directly from an experienced product marketing leader.

  • Work that ships and shows: your messaging, content, and launches reach the market fast and visibly. You'll see your impact, not just report on it.

  • Room to grow: this is a function we're investing in. Do great work and there's real room to rise.

If you love going deep with the builders shipping AI into enterprise applications and love making that technology make sense to the people who buy it, you'll feel at home here.

Why join us

  • Annual financial bonus depending on the company’s performance.

  • Flexible schedule and fully remote work.

  • Professional development resources.

  • LinkedIn Learning access.

  • Extra leave for Tiugo Day - our company’s foundation day and your birthday.

  • English lessons with a native speaker and an online language platform where you can learn English, Spanish, German, Italian and French.

  • Access to a mental health and well-being platform with 24/7 dedicated psychological support.

  • 2 weeks of paid parental leave for our contractors.

Overview

Bruker is one of the world’s leading analytical instrumentation companies enabling scientists to make breakthrough discoveries and develop new applications that improve the quality of human life. Our high-performance products and high-value life science and diagnostic solutions are trusted by leading businesses, institutes, and scientists worldwide. Today, more than 8,500 employees at over 90 locations are working on this permanent challenge to make the world a better place.

The Staff Scientific Product Marketing Manager for the spatial proteomics portfolio shapes market strategy and drives commercial success for Bruker’s spatial proteomics platforms by bridging science, product strategy, and go‑to‑market execution. With deep understanding of spatial proteomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, multiomics workflows, and translational research use cases, the Sr. Scientific Product Marketing Manager translates complex technical capabilities into clear, differentiated value propositions for pharma, biotech, and academic researchers, defining positioning, crafting the narrative, and equipping commercial teams with scientifically credible messaging, as well as developing and executing content pieces to communicate the product stories. The role works cross‑functionally with R&D, product management, commercial teams, and leadership to champion customer needs and advance adoption of the CellScape and GeoMx platforms. Ideal candidates thrive at the intersection of science, strategy, and storytelling, shaping market understanding of Bruker’s instruments to support spatial proteomics platforms across the full product lifecycle.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities:

  • Product Positioning & Messaging: Partner with Product Management and cross-functional teams to develop compelling positioning and messaging for the CellScape and GeoMx platforms. Clearly articulate each product’s value proposition and ensure consistent, accurate, and up-to-date messaging across all marketing channels. Maintain message integrity and alignment over time, minimizing inconsistencies across regions, campaigns, and content types.
  • Campaign & Content Execution: Execute integrated campaigns that support global marketing programs. Coordinate the development of content and creative assets, including social and digital materials, and manage release timing across channels. Monitor campaign performance and optimize based on engagement metrics and channel insights. Collaborate with marketing programs to deploy content through an omnichannel approach.
  • Go-to-Market & Lead Activation: Translate go-to-market strategies into actionable marketing plans that drive qualified leads and support sales pipeline growth. Manage lead generation efforts across campaigns, webinars, and events, including audience targeting and list sourcing from associations, conferences, and external partners.
  • Sales Enablement: Equip the commercial team with the tools, training and resources needed to effectively communicate the value of Bruker Spatial Biology products. Support the sales process by tailoring content to specific buyer personas and stages of the customer journey, helping to accelerate deal velocity and improve win rates.
  • Competitive Analysis and Market Research: Evaluate competitors' products, messaging, customers, publications, market share, features, and customer perceptions to gain actionable insights that inform strategic decisions and shape the messaging and positioning of Bruker Spatial Biology products. Provide periodic updates to the commercial team on recent developments from the competitors.
  • Performance Tracking & Reporting: Track and report on the performance of marketing initiatives. Analyze key metrics such as lead volume, conversion rates, and return on investment (ROI) to guide future program improvements.

Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Education: Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in life sciences, molecular biology, immunology, oncology, or a related field required.
  • Scientific Expertise: Strong working knowledge of molecular biology, sequencing, proteomics and multiomics approaches (RNA/protein), and spatial biology. Familiarity with spatial proteomics and high-plex proteomics technologies is highly desirable.
  • Marketing & Commercial Experience: 3-7+ years of experience in product marketing, product management, applications, or related commercial roles in the life sciences/tools industry. Experience developing product positioning, messaging, and go‑to‑market strategies for scientific instruments, assays, or software. Proven ability to partner with sales and applications teams to support field enablement and customer engagement.
  • Strategic & Analytical Skills: Ability to translate complex scientific concepts into clear, differentiated value propositions for multiple audience types. Strong market and competitive analysis skills and experience identifying customer needs and emerging trends. Demonstrated success in driving cross‑functional alignment and influencing without authority.
  • Communication & Content Development: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with ability to craft scientific yet commercially relevant materials. Experience developing marketing collateral, campaigns, presentations, and digital content is a plus.
  • Collaboration & Leadership: Effective at working across R&D, product management, sales, applications, and leadership teams. Ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize effectively, and drive initiatives from concept to execution.
  • Other Preferred Experience: Background working with biopharma, biotech startups, CROs, or translational research groups. Willingness to travel for customer visits, conferences, and internal company events, up to 15%.

At Bruker, base salary is part of our total compensation. The estimated base salary range for this full-time position is between $108,000 and $173,000 provides an opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base salary for the role will depend on a several job-related factors, including, but not limited to education, training, experience, the geographic location of the successful candidate, skills, competencies, job-related knowledge and travel requirements for this position. Full-time employees may also be eligible for a performance-related incentive in addition to a full range of benefits including 401(k) with company match, an employee stock purchase plan, medical and dental plans, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability insurance, employee assistance program and paid time off including vacation, sick time and holidays, and more.

Bruker is an equal-opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

jobs.excerpt: Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet.
jobs.description:
Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet. We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.

Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet. We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.

About the Opportunity

This isn't a role for someone waiting to be told what to build. We want a true self-starter: endlessly curious, genuinely ambitious, and humble enough to be trusted with real influence.

This person will own our internal systems integrations and the delivery of our MCP layer. You'll keep the lights on while identifying incremental improvements, and build the layer that enables the business to become builders and lets agents do real work safely. You'll spend time in both worlds, often in the same week, sometimes in the same day.

You're an enabler with a high level of ownership, ready to flex whatever muscle the day calls for. An integration breaks — you fix it. The business needs new functionality — you build it. Our MCP layer needs a new connection — you stand it up.

You think beyond the fix. We don't just want someone who keeps integrations running — we want someone who's constantly looking for the opportunity to simplify and consolidate them. You know the difference between patching something and rebuilding it onto better infrastructure, and you have a bias toward leaving every system you touch better than you found it, not just functional.

AI isn't an add-on here — it's how the work gets done. This is an AI-enabled role in an AI-enabled organization. You'll use AI tooling to write code, maintain the environment, and move faster across a wider surface area than one engineer could otherwise cover. It's not a tool you reach for occasionally; it's part of your everyday process.

We're just getting started building the infrastructure that lets everyone in the business become a builder. There's no finished playbook. Our MCP layer doesn't have an established pattern for security, access control, or agent tooling yet — you'll help write it, in partnership with the people who own the roadmap.

What You’ll Own

  • Back-office integrations — Maintain and enhance the integrations connecting NetSuite, HighJump, our data warehouse, and adjacent systems. Rebuild individual flows onto better infrastructure when it makes sense to, and know the difference between a fix and a rebuild. Go beyond maintenance to actively look for ways to simplify and consolidate our integration landscape — fewer moving parts, less duplicated logic, systems that are easier for the next person to reason about.
  • Grove Brain / internal MCP layer — Build Grove Brain out from its current early stage into a durable platform other teams build on. Design and implement the connectors and tools that let agents act on real Grove systems.
  • Security, access, and governance for agents — Help define and build how agents authenticate, what they're allowed to touch, and how that's audited, in partnership with the teams who own security and infrastructure rather than setting policy solo.
  • Hands-on enablement — Be the person a team calls when they're stuck mid-build on an integration or an agent problem, whether that's a connector, a permissions question, or a "we don't know what's possible yet" question.
  • Judgment calls — Decide when a systems problem is yours to solve and when it's actually a process problem that belongs to the business.
  • AI-assisted development — Use AI tooling aggressively as a force multiplier, and hold the line on quality while you do it. You should be moving noticeably faster than an engineer working without these tools, without your standards slipping. More on this below.
  • Craft, performance, and quality — Own performance, stability and maintainability in the code you ship, at the scale Grove actually runs at.

About You

  • 5+ years building and operating building and maintaining production system integrations — the kind that move data between platforms like NetSuite, HighJump, or similar ERP/WMS systems.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: you can design a pipeline, debug it under pressure, and know the difference between a quick fix and a real one.
  • Genuine hands-on experience with AI tools and, ideally, agent frameworks or MCP — not just familiarity, but a track record of building with them.
  • Comfortable operating with a rough direction instead of a finished spec, and you make real progress anyway.
  • A builder's mindset — you'd rather stand something up yourself than write a design doc for someone else to build.
  • Enough security instinct to ask the right questions about what an agent should and shouldn't be able to touch, even when you're not the final decision-maker on policy.
  • You're honest about what you don't know. You can say "I haven't worked with that" without flinching, and you don't paper over the gap with a confident guess.
  • Background with Airflow, Airbyte, or similar data-pipeline infrastructure
  • New technology doesn’t scare you. You’ve been dropped into an unfamiliar framework, language, or platform and gotten productive fast, and you can point to a time you did it. You evaluate new tools on the merits instead of defaulting to what you already know or chasing whatever is new.
  • You’re honest about what you don’t know. You can say “I haven’t worked with that” without flinching, and you don’t paper over the gap with a confident guess.
  • You’ve taken something vague, made it concrete, brought other people along, and shipped it.
  • You work well with others. You give direct feedback kindly, you take it well, and people want you on their project.
  • A real sense of ownership and pride in the experiences you ship and the code you leave behind.
  • You write things down, and people understand them. You can a non-technical person through a technical tradeoff without hiding behind jargon.
  • Genuine enthusiasm for Grove’s mission and sustainability values, not just the tech stack.

How We Work Together

  • This is a high trust environment. You’ll get real scope and real decisions early, and nobody is going to look over your shoulder while you do the work. Trust runs both directions: we’ll be straight with you about the business, the tradeoffs, and the parts of the codebase we aren’t proud of, and we expect that same candor back.
  • We value psychological safety first and foremost. It’s the precondition for everything else on this list. The teams that solve genuinely hard problems are the ones where people feel safe saying “I don’t understand this yet.”
  • “I haven’t worked with that” is a complete answer here. We have deep respect for an engineer who names the edge of their own knowledge instead of bluffing past it. We don’t need you to know everything. We need you to be honest about where your expertise begins and ends — and that honesty is worth more to us than a confident guess, in an interview and on the job.

How We think About AI

We’re serious about this, so we’d rather be direct than let you find out later.

  • AI tooling is part of how this team works every day, not an experiment on the side. We want someone who genuinely enjoys these tools and keeps getting better with them.
  • Nobody here has AI figured out, and we’re skeptical of anyone who says they do. The tooling changes month to month. We are all working it out together, in the open. We’d rather hire someone actively learning than someone with a methodology to evangelize.

  • The version of this we don’t want: code that ships because a model was confident. If you can’t explain why your code looks the way it does, “the model wrote it” isn’t an answer.
  • The version we do want: someone who moves twice as fast with these tools and whose standards didn’t move at all.
  • This is where honesty about the edges of your knowledge matters most. AI makes it effortless to produce work you don’t actually understand. Flagging that is a strength here, not an admission.

Our interview process includes a take-home project and a working review session that covers system design, coding, product thinking, and how you use AI. We’d rather see how you actually work than quiz you on algorithms — there’s no LeetCode round.

Title: Databricks Engineer

Location: Remote in USA

Working hours in EST

Required certification: Active Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate certification.

Role Summary

The Data Engineer is responsible for building, maintaining, and supporting data solutions on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform running on Microsoft Azure, AWS or GCP. The role leverages Databricks, Python, PySpark, and SQL to deliver data ingestion, transformation, modeling, and pipeline orchestration.

Working within the standards and designs set with the Senior Data Engineer, this role independently owns the delivery of assigned pipelines from development through production support.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain batch and streaming data pipelines for extracting, transforming, and loading (ETL/ELT) data from multiple sources into the Databricks lakehouse on Azure.
  • Implement data ingestion using Auto Loader, Lakeflow Connect, and Azure Data Factory.
  • Develop pipelines with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (formerly Delta Live Tables), including data quality expectations.
  • Perform data manipulation and transformation using PySpark and Spark SQL, ensuring data is prepared for analytics and reporting.
  • Configure, schedule, and monitor data workflows with Lakeflow Jobs (formerly Databricks Workflows).
  • Implement data models within the lakehouse following medallion architecture (bronze/silver/gold) and team modeling standards.
  • Apply Unity Catalog permissions and governance standards to the data assets you build.
  • Write unit and data quality tests and deploy pipelines through CI/CD using Git folders and Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles).
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and resolve pipeline failures and data quality issues in production.
  • Participate in code reviews and contribute to team documentation and engineering standards.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including business stakeholders and IT, to ensure data solutions meet business and performance requirements aligned to project goals.

Required Qualifications

Experience

  • 6+ years of professional experience in data engineering, data & analytics or data warehousing.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience working with Databricks in a data engineering capacity.
  • 3+ years of experience with Python, including manipulating large datasets using PySpark DataFrames, Spark SQL, and/or the pandas API on Spark.
  • 2+ years of data engineering experience on Microsoft Azure (e.g., ADLS Gen2, Azure Data Factory, Key Vault).

Skills and Knowledge

  • Proficiency in Python programming for data engineering tasks.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL for data modeling, transformation, and querying.
  • Working knowledge of Delta Lake fundamentals (e.g., MERGE, schema evolution, time travel).
  • Working knowledge of Unity Catalog concepts, including catalogs, schemas, and permissions.
  • Experience with Git-based version control and familiarity with CI/CD practices for data pipelines.
  • Understanding of testing and deployment strategies for data pipelines, including productionizing ETL pipelines and Databricks SQL queries.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, or a closely related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience implementing streaming data ingestion in Databricks (Structured Streaming, Auto Loader, Event Hubs).
  • Experience with healthcare data (e.g., claims, EHR/clinical data, HL7/FHIR) and HIPAA/PHI handling.
  • Exposure to Spark and Delta Lake performance tuning and compute cost optimization.
  • Familiarity with dimensional modeling and SCD Type 1 and Type 2 patterns.
  • Experience enabling BI consumption through Databricks SQL warehouses and tools such as Power BI.

The base salary for this position is $92,250 to $120,000 plus incentives that align with individual and company performance. Actual salaries will vary based on work location, qualifications, skills, education, experience, and competencies. Benefits available to eligible employees in this role include medical, dental, and vision insurance, comprehensive employee assistance program, 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off and holidays and paid learning days.

Quantum Computing Engineer

Location: Remote (Supporting Eastern Time Zone)
Employment Type: Full-Time
Security Requirement: Tier 4 / High Risk Background Investigation
Travel: Approximately two trips per year (seven trips over the life of the contract)

Salary Range: $200,000- $230,000

Position Overview

MKS2 is seeking a highly experienced Quantum Computing / Cryptography Engineer (Key Personnel) to support a federal government program focused on advancing cryptographic modernization, quantum computing readiness, and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) initiatives. This role will serve as a subject matter expert responsible for evaluating emerging quantum technologies, assessing cryptographic risks, developing quantum-resistant strategies, and supporting enterprise-wide migration planning for future cryptographic standards.

The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in quantum computing, cryptography, cybersecurity, and secure systems architecture, with experience supporting large-scale enterprise or government environments. This individual will work closely with technical teams, security leadership, and executive stakeholders to ensure organizational readiness for the evolving quantum computing landscape.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead assessments of organizational cryptographic systems and identify risks associated with advancements in quantum computing.
  • Develop quantum-resilient security strategies and migration roadmaps aligned with federal cybersecurity requirements.
  • Research, evaluate, and implement post-quantum cryptography (PQC) solutions and quantum-resistant algorithms.
  • Advise stakeholders on the impact of quantum computing technologies on enterprise security architectures.
  • Conduct cryptographic inventory assessments and prioritize systems for modernization and migration.
  • Evaluate emerging cryptographic standards and frameworks, including NIST post-quantum cryptography standards.
  • Design and test cryptographic solutions using classical and quantum simulation tools.
  • Provide technical guidance for implementing quantum-safe encryption, key management, and PKI solutions.
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity, software engineering, data science, and infrastructure teams to integrate quantum-resistant technologies.
  • Support policy development, governance activities, and strategic planning related to cryptographic modernization.
  • Prepare technical reports, executive briefings, and risk assessments for government stakeholders and leadership.
  • Participate in technical working groups, architecture reviews, and program management activities.

Required Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years of Information Technology experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years of Quantum Computing and Cryptography experience supporting large corporations or Federal Government agencies comparable in size and complexity to the GSA, IRS, DoD, or VA.
  • Experience supporting cryptographic modernization efforts and enterprise security initiatives.
  • Experience evaluating emerging quantum technologies and developing implementation strategies.
  • Experience working in project-based environments supporting large-scale technology initiatives.

Substitution:

  • A Master's degree in a related Information Technology field may substitute for up to two years of the required experience.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in one of the following fields:

  • Business Administration
  • Business Management
  • Cybersecurity
  • Computer Science
  • Information Systems
  • Information Assurance
  • Information Security
  • Information Resource Management
  • Related discipline

Required Certifications

Must possess one or more of the following certifications:

  • Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level III
  • Information Assurance Management (IAM) Level III
  • Information Assurance System Architect and Engineer (IASAE) Level III

Required Expertise

  • Strong understanding of quantum mechanics, quantum information theory, and quantum computing principles.
  • Expertise with quantum algorithms including Shor's Algorithm, Grover's Algorithm, and related quantum computational models.
  • Hands-on experience with quantum development platforms and frameworks such as:
    • IBM Qiskit
    • Google Cirq
    • Quipper
    • Microsoft Quantum Development Kit
  • Extensive knowledge of cryptographic protocols including RSA, AES, and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI).
  • Expertise in post-quantum cryptography, quantum-resistant algorithms, and cryptographic modernization initiatives.
  • Knowledge of cryptographic standards and compliance frameworks including NIST and ISO/IEC 19790.
  • Proficiency in Python, C++, Java, or similar programming languages used for implementing and testing cryptographic solutions.
  • Experience utilizing classical and quantum simulation environments.
  • Proven ability to develop and advise on cryptographic migration strategies aligned with post-quantum security requirements.
  • Experience assessing enterprise cryptographic inventories and prioritizing modernization efforts.
  • Ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts and quantum-related risks to executive leadership and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience developing policy recommendations and technical guidance aligned with NIST PQC standards, including FIPS 203, FIPS 204, and FIPS 205.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills with experience operating within structured program environments.

Security Requirement

  • Must be able to successfully obtain and maintain a Tier 4 / High Risk Background Investigation.

Place of Performance

  • Remote position supporting Eastern Time Zone operations.
  • Meetings and coordination activities may occur at the Department of Veterans Affairs Central Office (VACO), 811 Vermont Avenue NW, Washington, DC.
  • Routine onsite support is not anticipated.

Hours of Operation

  • Available during normal Federal Government workdays.
  • Responsive during core business hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern Time.

Travel Requirements

  • Support program-related meetings, workshops, and stakeholder engagements as required.
  • Government estimates approximately two trips per year, totaling seven trips across the life of the contract.

Why Join MKS2?

MKS2 delivers innovative technology and cybersecurity solutions that support critical federal missions. As a Quantum Computing / Cryptography Engineer, you will play a key role in helping government organizations prepare for the future of cybersecurity by developing strategies and solutions that address the emerging challenges posed by quantum computing. This position offers the opportunity to influence enterprise-wide security modernization efforts within a highly collaborative, mission-driven environment.

Our Finance team plays a central role in maintaining the rigorous financial integrity that a regulated payments business demands, across multiple legal entities, currencies, and compliance frameworks.

About the Role

We're looking for a highly technical and detail-oriented Senior Accountant to join our growing Finance team. This role is ideal for someone with strong financial accounting fundamentals, audit experience, and a continuous improvement mindset who enjoys building scalable, efficient processes in a fast-moving environment.

You'll play a key role in supporting month-end close, financial reporting, payroll, audits, and process optimization across the organization. We're looking for someone who not only understands accounting deeply, but also actively looks for ways to improve how work gets done through automation, systems thinking, and operational efficiency.

An interest in emerging technologies, including AI and workflow automation, is considered a strong asset.

What You'll Do

Financial Reporting & Entity Management

  • Own core month-end and year-end close activities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, accruals, and financial reporting
  • Manage the full-cycle accounts payable (AP) process, including vendor invoice coding, approvals, and payment runs
  • Prepare and review revenue recognition entries, including treatment of deferred revenue
  • Maintain and reconcile prepaid expenses, fixed assets, and other balance sheet schedules, ensuring accurate amortization/depreciation and supporting documentation
  • Help maintain rigorous separation of trust (client funds) and operating accounts in compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policy
  • Support financial exposure reporting related to payment losses, chargebacks, and disputes; collaborate with Risk and Operations to quantify and track losses
  • Monitor foreign exchange exposure across multi-currency entities and support hedging documentation

Compliance, Controls & Audit

  • Design and help strengthen the internal controls framework across accounting processes, with particular attention to segregation of duties and payment fund safeguarding
  • Support the year-end audit, SR&ED submission, tax filings, and other regulatory reporting obligations
  • Help ensure ASPE/IFRS compliance and assist in keeping accounting policies up to date for all entities
  • Proactively flag control gaps and support remediation efforts before they become audit findings
  • Support North American payroll operations, including payroll accounting, reconciliations, and compliance considerations

Automation & Process Efficiency

  • Support the accounting tech stack; help evaluate and optimize tools (Xero, Plooto, and beyond) to eliminate manual effort and increase accuracy
  • Partner with Business Intelligence and Engineering to help automate reconciliations, reporting, and close processes
  • Support the FinOps best-practices group, helping govern and optimize variable usage-based costs such as cloud and infrastructure spend

Team Leadership & Stakeholder Management → Stakeholder Support

  • Partner with FP&A on internal and investor reporting, ensuring accounting outputs are investor-ready
  • Act as a point of contact for external auditors, tax advisors, banking partners, and payment processors as needed

What You Bring

  • 3+ years of accounting experience
  • CPA designation or actively pursuing CPA completion
  • Strong technical accounting knowledge with a focus on financial accounting and audit support
  • Strong knowledge of ASPE and IFRS; experience in tech or payments SaaS strongly preferred
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Demonstrated interest in process improvement, automation, and scalable finance operations
  • Comfort working in evolving, fast-paced environments with shifting priorities
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A natural problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
  • Interest in AI, automation tools, or modern finance technology considered an asset

What Success Looks Like

  • Accurate, timely financial reporting and close processes
  • Strong audit readiness and technical accounting support
  • Improved efficiency through automation and process optimization
  • Reliable payroll and AP operations with strong controls and no material errors
  • A proactive approach to identifying and solving operational challenges
  • Strong working relationships with FP&A, Risk, Operations, and other cross-functional partners

Compensation & Inclusion

Plooto is committed to building an inclusive and equitable workplace. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences.

In accordance with Ontario hiring requirements, accommodation is available throughout the recruitment process upon request.
